# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Age:** An old woman  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014)</sub>
- **Status:** Widow  <sub>[v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014), [v3 c19 P5](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper for college students  <sub>[v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Titles:** Aunt Jamesina  <sub>[v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v3 c4 P45](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0045)</sub>; Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with pink cheeks, large, soft blue eyes, and snow-white hair worn in dainty puffs over her ears. She is neat and old-fashioned in her dress, often wearing a fluffy white shawl over her shoulders. Her face is described as softly triangular, with youthful and mirthful eyes.

_Sources: [v3 c11 P42](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0042), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina possesses a bright, cheerful, and youthful spirit that belie her years, believing in indulging herself in old-fashioned opinions and comfortable ways. She has an active sense of humor, a soft heart, and an open, indulgent attitude toward young people. Though devout and respectful of religious duties, she is tolerant and prefers to let the girls manage their own affairs rather than scold or supervise them strictly. She is also an animal lover who refuses to abandon stray cats.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P1](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0001), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P63](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0063), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001), [v3 c25 P10](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0010)_

## Goals

- To keep house comfortably for the girls at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001)</sub>

## History

After her daughter married and left for foreign mission work, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house until her niece, Stella Maynard, invited her to keep house for a group of Redmond students at Patty's Place in Kingsport. She accepted and took along her two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph. At Patty's Place, she presided over the household with gentle humor and warm-heartedness, accommodating Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon. She also took in Rusty, a stray cat that Anne rescued, and insisted on staying at Patty's Place over the Christmas holidays rather than leave the animals alone. At the end of the girls' college years, she decided to take all three cats to live with her at Green Gables to keep Marilla Cuthbert company when Anne left for her teaching position.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P56](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0056), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001), [v3 c38 P8](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0008)_

## Background by volume

- Named Jamesina after her father James, who was drowned at sea a month before she was born  <sub>[v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014)</sub>
- Had a daughter named Elizabeth who became a foreign missionary in India  <sub>[v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>
- Had several suitors in her youth, including Jim Elwood, Dan Winston, Milton Edwards, and Horatio Reeve  <sub>[v3 c35 P25](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0025)</sub>

> You can all go to destruction in your own way.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> Thank goodness air and salvation are still free.  <sub>[v3 c17 P4](../source/v03-c17.md#nw-v03-c17-p0004)</sub>

> Never write a line you would be ashamed to read at your own funeral.  <sub>[v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time.  <sub>[v3 c19 P5](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0005)</sub>
